threads.thread_goal: Align on pilot scope, roles and initial household targeting approach.

messages.text: Hi team, welcome to the channel for our Community Food Support Pilot! I've attached the overview document, A1, which outlines the main goals. Please have a read when you can. Let's start by discussing the overall scope and how we define success for this 6-week pilot. Also keen to hear initial thoughts on T1, specifically the eligibility criteria for households.

Thanks for setting this up. I've reviewed A1. For success criteria, I suggest we focus on three measurable points: 1) Number of households consistently supported each week, 2) Zero food safety incidents, and 3) Positive feedback from at least 75% of participants via the doorstep check-ins. This gives us a clear target.

Those are solid metrics. On T1, for eligibility, we should prioritize households not currently receiving other food aid to avoid duplication and reach the most isolated. We could use referrals from our community partners as the primary source, with a simple check question. This also helps manage privacy from the start.
Document read. The scope seems manageable for 6 weeks. The success criteria from @44809 make sense from an operational standpoint, especially the food safety metric.

Great points, everyone. I like the focus on measurable outcomes and the idea of using partner referrals for T1. How many households should we aim for? The document A1 is a bit vague on the exact number.
How do we find the families? Do we just knock on doors?

Good question @516425. As @534740 suggested, we'll work with local community organisations who already know the families that need support. They will provide us with a list of interested households, so we won't be cold-calling. For the pilot, I'd suggest starting with 15-20 households. It's a manageable number to test our routes and processes without being overwhelming.
ok that makes sense. 20 sounds like a lot for deliveries.
We can cluster them into 2-3 small delivery routes. We'll tackle that in T4. For now, agreeing on the number is the key step.
Okay, there seems to be consensus building. Let's formalize this. Are we all agreed on the proposed success criteria and the initial target of 15-20 households identified via partners?

Yes, I'm in agreement. To summarize:
1. Success criteria: Consistent support for 15-20 households, zero food safety incidents, 75%+ positive feedback. (D1)
2. Eligibility: Households referred by community partners, not currently receiving other food aid, with a target of 15-20 for the pilot. (D2)
Agreed.
Confirm. This gives us a clear foundation.
ok

Perfect, decisions D1 and D2 are locked in. Thanks for the clear summary, @44809. I will take the lead on T1 to coordinate with our community partners and get that initial list drawn up. I'll aim to have a draft by end of day tomorrow.
Great. Let me know if you need a hand with drafting the communication to the partners. My experience in that area might be useful.
That would be very helpful, thank you! I'll send you a draft to review.
While you work on T1, I can start thinking about the tracking and labelling system (T7) to make sure we have a robust way to handle the anonymised IDs from the start.

threads.thread_goal: Design and agree on the end-to-end operational flow from surplus collection to delivery.

messages.text: Morning all. Let's talk about the operational flow. I've started a draft process for T2, covering collection and initial sorting. The main steps are: 1. Collect surplus from warehouse. 2. Transport to sorting area. 3. Sort into categories (fresh, ambient, chilled). 4. Log items. What are your thoughts on this, and how can we best integrate the packing (T6) and delivery prep (T4)?

This is a good start. For T2, I'd add a crucial step between 3 and 4: 'Quality & Date Check'. We must ensure everything is well within its use-by date. For T6, I can create a simple packing checklist (A3) that specifies the target mix of items for a standard parcel. This will ensure consistency. We can then have a dedicated packing station right after the sorting area.

Excellent point, the date check is non-negotiable. I'll add that in. A checklist for packing (A3) sounds perfect, that will standardize the process and make it faster. I'll also make sure the sorting area layout reflects this flow. We must adhere to the food safety guide A2 at all stages.
When do I pick up the parcels for delivery? I need to know the schedule so I can plan my regular mail route.

That's the key hand-off point. I suggest we have a fixed 'dispatch window'. For example, all parcels for the day are packed and ready for collection by 10 AM every Tuesday and Thursday. This gives @516425 a predictable schedule for T4 and ensures parcels don't sit around.
A fixed schedule is a great idea. Tuesdays and Thursdays at 10 AM sounds like a good starting point. @516425, would that work for you?
Yes 10am is fine. How many deliveries will be on each day?
We can split the 15-20 households across the two days, so roughly 8-10 per day. For T4, you can plan one efficient route for each day. We can test and optimize this during the dry run.

Okay, so let's refine the process. The full flow would be: Collect -> Transport -> Sort (by type) -> Quality/Date Check -> Log Items -> Pack Parcels (using A3) -> Stage for Dispatch. This seems like a solid, auditable process. Are we happy to approve this as our standard procedure?
Looks complete and logical. I approve.
Me too. This covers all the bases. Let's lock that in.
Agreed. And for the schedule, we're confirming: Deliveries on Tuesdays and Thursdays, with parcels ready for pickup by @516425 at 10 AM. He will own the route planning for T4. Is that correct?
Yes, I can do that.
Excellent. That's our second decision made. Thanks all for getting this sorted so efficiently.
Great. I'll get a first draft of the packing checklist A3 for T6 done by tomorrow morning for everyone to review.
And I will formally document the approved process for T2 today.
I will look at the routes for T4.
Perfect. Let us know if you need any help with the mapping tool, @516425.
This schedule also helps me finalize the tracking sheet design, as I can build in columns for 'Tue' and 'Thu' batches.
Good thinking, that integration will be key.
Process for T2 is now drafted and saved in the shared folder. Ready for review when you have a moment.

threads.thread_goal: Finalise safety, privacy and doorstep interaction guidelines.

messages.text: Hi all, moving on to our interaction guidelines. I've put together a first draft of the Doorstep Script (A4) based on the requirements for T5. At the same time, @429831 has shared the Food Safety Guide (A2) for T3. Can everyone please review both documents and share your feedback?

Thanks for sharing. For the Food Safety Guide (A2), I've tried to keep it simple with clear do's and don'ts. The key points are temperature control for chilled items and strict hand hygiene. I've cross-referenced it with our internal compliance rules.

Thanks. The safety guide A2 looks great - clear and concise. For the doorstep script A4, the tone is good. I'd suggest one change: instead of asking 'Do you need any other help?', which can be a closed question, we could try 'Is there anything else on your mind today?'. It's more open and less intrusive, encouraging a real conversation if the person is comfortable.

That's a much better phrasing. It aligns with the goal of a 'wellbeing check' rather than a service assessment. On A2, I have one question: it mentions logging temperatures. Where will this be recorded? We should ensure it's part of the main log sheet for traceability.
Good catch. We can add a temperature check column to the main collection log. I'll coordinate with you on that for the log template.
I love that suggestion for the script, @44809. It's much more empathetic. I'll update A4 with that wording. Any other thoughts on the script or the safety guide?
I'm a bit nervous about asking people questions. What if they tell me something serious? I'm not a social worker.

That's a very valid concern, @516425. The script in A4 is designed to keep the conversation light. The goal isn't to solve problems at the doorstep. It's just to listen. The script includes a line for you to say: 'Thank you for sharing that with me. I'll make a note for our support team to follow up'. Your only job is to pass the information on, not to act on it yourself. We'll cover this in the training session (T9).
Ok, that helps. So I just write it down.
Exactly. Thanks for clarifying that, @44809. It seems we have a clear path forward. With the temperature log addition, are we ready to sign off on the Food Safety Guide A2?
Yes, I'm happy with it. I'll make that small addition and then it's final.
Approved from my side.
Great, that's D5 confirmed. Now for the doorstep script A4. With the wording change suggested by @44809, are there any other objections to finalizing it?
None from me. It feels balanced and respectful.
It's ok.
Wonderful. Then we have our decision. I'll publish the final version of A4 today.
I'll finalize A2 for T3 now.

threads.thread_goal: Set up tracking, labelling and logging tools before the dry run.

messages.text: Hi team, I've created draft versions of the tracking and logging tools for T7 and T8. Please see the Household and Route Tracking Sheet (A5) and the Delivery and Outreach Log (A6). My proposal for the labelling scheme is a simple alphanumeric code: 'CFS' for Community Food Support, followed by a two-digit household number, e.g., 'CFS-01', 'CFS-02'. This code will be used on all parcels and logs, with no personal names or addresses on the labels themselves. A5 will be the master sheet linking the code to the delivery address, which only the core team can access. Feedback is welcome.

This is excellent, @534740. Clean, simple, and prioritizes privacy. The separation of the master sheet A5 from the daily log A6 is a critical control. The 'CFS-XX' format is perfect. I've reviewed both templates and they look ready to go. This system is robust.

Wow, this is fantastic work. It perfectly addresses the privacy constraints. The coding system is clear and easy to follow. I've checked A6 and it has a good column for brief, non-sensitive notes from the doorstep chats. This is exactly what we need.
From a packing perspective, this is great. We just need to write one simple code on each box. Easy to manage and low risk of errors.
So on my delivery sheet I will see the code and the address? And the box only has the code?

Precisely, @516425. You will get a daily route sheet printed from A5 that has both the code and the address for your deliveries. The parcel itself will only have the 'CFS-XX' code. This way, if a parcel is misplaced, it can't be traced back to a specific person or address.
ok i get it now. thanks.
It seems like everyone is on board with this proposal. It's clear, secure, and efficient. Are we all happy to formally approve this labelling and coding scheme?
Yes, fully support it. Let's lock it in.
Yes, it's good to go.
yes
Great, D7 is confirmed. Thank you @534740 for putting together such a thorough and well-thought-out system. This is a huge step forward.
Happy to help. I'll finalize the templates for A5 and A6 and save them as the master versions in our shared drive. That completes T7 and T8.
With this in place, we are officially ready for the dry run next week (T10). I'll schedule the pre-briefing session (T9) for Monday morning.
Looking forward to it. Having these solid processes and tools in place will make the dry run much more effective.

threads.thread_goal: Review dry run results and agree adjustments and next steps.

messages.text: Hi team, we've completed our one-week dry run (T10). A big thank you to everyone for your hard work! I've reviewed the Operational Issues Log (A7) and wanted to discuss the key findings and decide on our next steps. Overall it went well, but there were a few learning points.
The route on Tuesday took longer than I thought. The traffic on Green Street was bad. I was 20 minutes late for the last two drops.

From the packing side, we had a minor issue. The chilled goods box from the warehouse was left out for about 15 minutes before we could log it, so the temperature was slightly high. I've logged this in A7. We need a better hand-off process with the warehouse team.

Thanks for flagging those points. For the delivery route, @516425, we can easily adjust. Let's re-order the Tuesday route to do Green Street first, or build in a 30-minute buffer. For the temperature issue, I suggest we implement a rule that chilled goods are not brought to the packing area until we are physically ready to process them. It's a simple process tweak.

The logging process worked smoothly. The CFS-XX codes were easy to use. One suggestion for the Outreach Log (A6): could we add a simple checkbox column for 'Follow-up needed'? It would make it easier for @357710 to quickly scan for actions during the weekly monitoring (T11).

That's a brilliant idea for the log, @534740. It would make T11 much more efficient. I'll add that column. And the proposed solutions for the route timing and the chilled goods hand-off sound very practical. Are there any other issues or suggestions from the dry run?
Doing Green Street first is a good idea. I can try that.
Yes, the new rule for chilled goods makes sense. I'll communicate that to the warehouse staff.

The doorstep interactions went well. The updated script from A4 was very effective. Most people were happy to have a quick chat. No major concerns were raised, which is a positive sign for the pilot's approach.

That's great to hear. It sounds like we've identified some minor, fixable issues and the core process is sound. So, the big question: based on this, are we confident to proceed with the full 6-week pilot with these adjustments in place?

Yes, absolutely. The dry run did exactly what it was supposed to do: it stress-tested our system and revealed small friction points we can now smooth out. I propose we formally agree on the process changes and give the go-ahead for the full roll-out.
I concur. The system is stable and the proposed tweaks are minor. We are ready.
Agreed. Let's move forward.
yes i think so

Excellent! Decision D8 is made: we are a 'go' for the full pilot, starting next Tuesday. I'll document these agreed adjustments. My main task now is the weekly monitoring (T11), and for all of us, to keep the logs updated so we have great data for the final report (A8/T12). Well done everyone!
I'll update the A6 template with the new checkbox column now.
Let's make sure we capture all these learnings for the end-of-pilot summary A8. This is valuable insight.
Absolutely. I've started a draft of A8 already to collect these points as we go.
